description: Makes `null` and `undefined` distinct types that must be handled explicitly. Enabled by `strict`.
Falls back only when the left side is `null` or `undefined`, unlike `||` which also replaces `0`, `''` and `false`.
Removes `null | undefined` from a type without any runtime check. A wrong assertion crashes at runtime.
Return type for functions whose result must be ignored. `() => void` function types accept callbacks that return values.
The empty type: functions that always throw, and branches that cannot happen. Assignable to every type.
